title: Esme and the Lost Sparkly Button
markdown:
The moonlight made Esme’s room glow like a soft silvery cloud. In her sand tray lay scattered metal pieces, a quiet puzzle for sleepy eyes. She tried making her spoon stick to a shiny bit. It slid away. The night held still. Curtains breathed. Somewhere a cricket practised the same small note.

A soft Maa-maa floated in from the garden. Tumble the goat, big brown eyes worried. “Oh, Tumble. What’s the matter?” He nudged his woolly pocket. “Lost sparkly,” he bleated, a little tremble. His favourite sparkly button.

They did not rush. Moonlight lay on the tray like spilled milk. A moth considered the window and chose the garden instead. Esme waited with him, the way you wait when a friend is missing something small and important.

Tumble ambled over. As he sniffed near a smooth pebble, his little bell nudged something dark and grey — a quiet stone. Then the stone seemed to reach, and two metal pieces jumped toward it. They clicked gently against its surface. Tumble blinked. Esme’s eyes widened. “They’re sticking.”

She picked up the dark grey stone. Held it near a soft feather. A smooth pebble. Nothing. Near the metal pieces — click. They jumped and clung. She remembered the button. “Tumble, what was your button made of?”

He thought. “Shiny! Like… those bits!”

Esme held the stone — a magnet — close to Tumble’s pocket. Nestled deep within, the lost sparkly button came out on a gentle tug. Tumble gave a happy Maaa and nudged her cheek.

“A magnet,” Esme said, voice low and dreamy. “It pulls certain metal things toward it. Like your button. Not the feather. Not the pebble.”

Mrs Quinn’s soft knock came and went at the garden gate. She had been bringing a tin of biscuits, saw the button home in Tumble’s pocket, and smiled without coming in. The biscuits stayed on the step for morning. The night kept its hush.

Tumble munched clover, sparkle safe. Esme yawned. She snuggled into pillows, Tumble a warm sleepy presence nearby. The magnet rested on the little table, ordinary as a stone and not ordinary at all. Their breathing grew slow, and they drifted toward star-filled dreams, one quiet pull already finished for the night.
characters: Esme (a star gazer), Tumble (a goat), Quinn (a neighbor)
author: StoryGen Community
